title: BeaconPoint Health - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on private VPC deployment options. Customer has strict data residency and network isolation requirements; evaluating Redwood Private with AWS VPC peering or PrivateLink. Discussed overlapping CIDR, transit connectivity, region availability, audit/KMS integration, and pilot next steps.
topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway
Overlapping CIDR handling and IP planning
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we, uh, we're Maya from Redwood, account exec, and Samir our SE is here. Quick intros?
[00:08] Rob (BeaconPoint): Rob here, I'm the IT architect, Priya is our security lead, Ethan's our platform engineer, Aisha product.
[00:14] Maya: Awesome. Goal for today is to understand your network constraints and what a Private deployment would look like. We'll cover VPC peering, private endpoints, regions, and next steps.
[00:27] Samir (Redwood SE): Just to set expectations, Redwood Private gives you a private control plane and option for customer-managed networking. For AWS we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink/Private Endpoints; also Transit Gateway patterns for multi-account setups.
[00:40] Priya (BeaconPoint): Important note up front: all PHI must stay in our AWS accounts in us-east-1 and us-west-2, and we want no internet egress for inference traffic. Also KMS keys must be customer-managed.
[00:52] Maya: Totally, that's pretty standard for healthcare customers. We can pin deployments to specific regions and support customer-managed KMS. We'll dig into the KMS flow and audit integration in a minute.
[01:03] Ethan: What about the connectivity pattern? We currently use Transit Gateway between our VPCs and on-prem via VPN. Would Redwood require peering into a specific VPC?
[01:12] Samir: There are a few options. One: VPC peering between your inference VPC and our private worker VPC — low latency but requires non-overlapping CIDR and direct peering. Two: AWS PrivateLink / interface endpoints — we host the service endpoints in your account and you connect via ENIs, that avoids peering but has different egress/billing. Three: Transit Gateway attachments — if you already use TGW that's often simplest for multi-account routing.
[01:36] Rob: Hmm, we have overlapping 10.0.0.0/16 ranges across accounts. That would break peering.
[01:41] Samir: Right, peering requires unique CIDR ranges. For overlapping spaces PrivateLink is usually the recommended path because it doesn't require route table changes or unique CIDRs, it presents an ENI and private DNS.
[01:52] Priya: With PrivateLink, does data ever touch Redwood's public network? We're trying to avoid any public egress or third-party network hops.
[02:01] Samir: With AWS PrivateLink, traffic stays on the AWS network the whole way; the endpoint lives in your VPC and talks to our NLB in a managed VPC — there's no traversal over the public internet. For extra assurance we can provide architecture diagrams and network flow captures.
[02:16] Aisha: Are there any limits on model size or inference latency when using Private deployments?
[02:22] Samir: Not really from the networking perspective. Latency depends on region placement and instance types. For low-latency use cases we can co-locate in the same AZ/region and use dedicated GPU pools. We'll share our performance profiles.
[02:34] Rob: We also have strict egress logging and want all audit logs forwarded into our Splunk/S3. Can we get Redwood logs into our S3 bucket or CloudWatch?
[02:44] Maya: Yes, we support audit log forwarding. For Private deployments we can push logs to a customer-managed S3 or CloudWatch via cross-account role, and you can ingest into Splunk. We'll need to scope the retention and exact events.
[02:56] Priya: KMS — we need CMK that we control and that Redwood can't export. Can you support envelope encryption with our CMK?
[03:04] Samir: Yes, customer-managed CMKs are supported for data-at-rest. For in-flight requests we don't cache unencrypted blobs. We'll share our KMS integration playbook. There are some nuances around key policies for cross-account usage.
[03:17] Ethan: About IP allowlists — we have a private subnet where our services call model endpoints. Do you provide static IPs for egress or do we need NAT?
[03:26] Samir: If you're using PrivateLink, your VPC ENI connects directly; no NAT needed for calls to the endpoint. For calls outbound from our workers (e.g., to an external data source) we can put them in your managed NAT/VPC egress path if required, but typically data flows inbound from your network into Redwood.
[03:41] Rob: Does Redwood require any inbound firewall rules from our side?
[03:45] Samir: For PrivateLink, you create the interface endpoint in your account and it initiates the connection; so minimal inbound changes. If using VPC peering, you'd adjust route tables and security groups to allow the specific CIDR ranges.
[03:56] Maya: Quick note on regions — we run Private control planes in select regions; currently us-east-1 and us-west-2 are supported for early customers. Which region do you prefer?
[04:06] Priya: Prefer us-east-1 for data residency but some workloads in us-west-2.
[04:10] Maya: We can stand up a dual-region pilot or pin a deployment to us-east-1 and then expand. We'll confirm region availability in our follow-up.
[04:18] Aisha: Timeline—if we wanted to pilot in 6 weeks, what's needed?
[04:22] Maya: Typically 4–8 weeks for a pilot: legal/security review, account provisioning, networking setup (PrivateLink/TGW), and a small benchmark run. We can fast-track the networking if you provide an infra contact.
[04:34] Rob: Who from our side needs to be involved for the networking setup?
[04:37] Samir: Ideally your platform eng and network infra engineer — Ethan looks like the right person — plus a security reviewer for KMS/policies. We'll provide a prebuilt CloudFormation/Terraform template for PrivateLink and TGW attachments.
[04:49] Priya: Does Redwood manage any of the AWS accounts or do we keep full control?
[04:54] Samir: You keep full control. For Private deployments the customer-managed VPCs remain in your account; Redwood asks for specific role ARNs for cross-account access where needed, but you retain control over keys and networking.
[05:06] Rob: Any known gotchas? For instance, egress charges or restrictions on cross-region endpoints?
[05:11] Samir: Egress charges are AWS-native and depend on your architecture. If you cross regions, inter-region data transfer applies. PrivateLink has per-GB charges from AWS; peering does not have per-endpoint interface charges but requires non-overlapping CIDR. We'll include an estimated cost comparison in the follow-up.
[05:25] Maya: Ok let's talk success criteria for the pilot — what would make this a win for BeaconPoint?
[05:31] Aisha: 1) All PHI stays in our accounts and is encrypted with our CMK, 2) latency under 120ms p95 for our main inference route, 3) audit logs forwarded and visible in Splunk, 4) no public internet egress for inference traffic.
[05:45] Maya: Great, we can scope that. We'll plan a benchmark and end-to-end test for latency and log forwarding.
[05:52] Rob: Security checklist — we need SOC 2 report, penetration test summary, and network flow diagrams.
[05:58] Maya: We'll send SOC 2 cert and a summary of pen test results, plus the architecture diagram.
[06:04] Samir: Small technical point — if you want to validate performance we can run a local benchmark job that simulates your workload (sequence lengths, concurrency). We'll coordinate to get sample prompts and expected throughput.
[06:16] Ethan: For the benchmark, we have a 1k token average context, concurrent 20 qps, p95 latency requirement. Also would love to test quantized models if that changes throughput.
[06:27] Samir: Perfect — we'll include quantized variants and expected throughput tradeoffs.
[06:32] Priya: Legal — do you require a BAA?
[06:35] Maya: For PHI-containing workloads we offer BAA as part of the enterprise package. We'll flag legal to follow up.
[06:41] Aisha: Any integration work for SSO? We use SAML SSO and SCIM for identity provisioning.
[06:47] Maya: We support SAML and SCIM for RBAC. For Private deployments we can integrate with your IdP.
[06:52] Rob: Ok next steps?
[06:54] Maya: I'll summarize, but first any more questions?
[06:57] Priya: One more — how are software updates handled for Private? Do you push runtime updates?
[07:03] Samir: For Private we have an ops model: Redwood can push control plane updates; the customer controls worker images if desired, or we can manage worker updates under a maintenance window. We'll document the upgrade process.
[07:15] Maya: Alright recap and action items coming up. Thanks all.
[07:19] Rob: Thanks everyone.
